costGuide.title: BMW S63B44T2 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an S63B44T2 typically takes 14-18 hours at £75-£85/hr (independent M specialist) - main dealer rates are typically 50-70% higher. The hot‑vee design adds complexity to many repairs.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is whether the unit has had the valve stem seals addressed, the condition of the twin turbochargers (which sit in the hot‑vee and are labour‑intensive to access), and whether the cooling system has been proactively maintained. The 567 bhp vs 575 bhp output difference is simply a model‑specific calibration and does not affect replacement cost. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for more detail.

failures.title: BMW S63B44T2 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Oil Leaks - valve cover gaskets and oil supply system
items.whatHappens: Oil leaks are one of the most frequently reported issues on the S63 engine family. The hot‑vee design means the turbochargers sit in the valley between cylinder banks, subjecting gaskets and seals to significant heat cycling. Valve cover gaskets are a common failure point, with oil seeping onto the exhaust manifolds and producing a burning oil smell - a symptom many owners report. The oil pump intake snorkel was also revised on the S63B44T2 specifically for track use, to ensure oil supply even under high lateral and longitudinal acceleration.
items.repairVsReplace: Valve cover gasket replacement typically resolves the issue (£800-£1,500 at an independent specialist). If ignored, oil leaks can lead to low oil levels and eventual engine damage. Catastrophic oil starvation from a failed oil pump or severe leak can write off the engine - replacement is the only option. Read our full oil leak guide

items.title: Cooling System Stress - water pump, radiator, and coolant pipe failures
items.whatHappens: The S63B44T2 generates significant heat due to its hot‑vee turbo configuration and high power output. The cooling system - including the water pump, radiator, and various coolant pipes - is under considerable stress. Coolant leaks from the crossover pipes and water pump failures are known issues on high‑mileage S63 engines.
items.repairVsReplace: Water pump and thermostat replacement typically resolves the issue (£500-£1,200 at an independent specialist). If overheating is ignored, head gasket failure or cylinder head damage can occur - at which point a full engine replacement becomes the more economical route. Read our full cooling system failure guide

items.title: Valve Stem Seal Wear - oil consumption and smoke on startup
items.whatHappens: The S63 engine family - like its N63 predecessor - can suffer from valve stem seal wear, leading to oil consumption and blue smoke on cold starts. This is a well‑documented issue on the S63 platform. The TU2 revision improved some aspects of the lubrication system, but the issue can still present on higher‑mileage units.
items.repairVsReplace: Valve stem seal replacement is a significant job (£1,500-£3,000) due to the hot‑vee design requiring substantial disassembly. If caught early, the repair is viable; if ignored, carbon buildup and catalytic converter damage can occur, potentially requiring a full engine replacement.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the S63B44T2
variants.intro: The S63B44T2 (also designated S63R) is the second Technical Update of BMW's S63 engine, produced from 2015 to 2019. It is commonly confused with: | Similar Code | What It Is | Link | |---|---|---| | S63B44O0 | First‑generation S63 (2010-2013) - 547 bhp, fitted to E70 X5 M, E71 X6 M | BMW S63B44O0 engine | | S63B44T1 | First Technical Update (2011-2017) - 553 bhp, fitted to F10 M5, F12/F13 M6 | BMW S63B44T1 engine | | S63B44T3 | Third Technical Update (2018-present) - 591-617 bhp, fitted to F90 M5, M8, F95 X5 M, F96 X6 M | BMW S63B44T3 engine | | N63B44 | Standard 4.4L V8 - non‑M, fitted to 50i models; shares the block but lacks forged internals and M‑specific calibration | BMW N63B44 engine | How to find your engine code: The engine code is stamped on a metal plate on the cylinder block, visible from the driver's side of the engine bay, and also appears on the V5C registration document and in the vehicle's VIN (digits 4‑7). If you're unsure, enter your registration above - we'll confirm your exact fitment. Why the difference matters: The S63B44T2 produces 567-575 bhp - a significant increase over the 547 bhp of the original S63 and 553 bhp of the T1. Fitting an earlier S63 into a T2‑spec vehicle is not a straight swap; the ECU calibration, turbocharger hardware, and cooling system plumbing differ. The S63B44T2 also features revised connecting rods with improved lubrication channels, addressing earlier bearing wear concerns.

relatives.description: - the first Technical Update S63 (2011-2017) fitted to F10 M5 and F12/F13 M6; it produces 553 bhp and lacks the T2's revised connecting rods and track‑focused oil pump intake. If you have an earlier M5 or M6, this is the engine you need - but note it is not a direct swap into F85/F86 chassis due to different engine mounts and cooling system plumbing.

- the original S63 (2010-2013) with 547 bhp, fitted to E70 X5 M and E71 X6 M; it's the least powerful of the S63 family and the most prone to the early hot‑vee teething issues. If you're considering a used replacement for an F85/F86, avoid this earlier generation - it won't be a direct fit.

- the third Technical Update S63 (2018-present) producing 591-617 bhp, fitted to F90 M5, F91/F92/F93 M8, F95 X5 M and F96 X6 M; it introduced additional refinements including higher‑pressure fuel injection and revised turbocharger hardware. This engine is not backwards‑compatible with the T2's ECU or cooling system.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement S63B44T2 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used S63B44T2 can make sense for owners facing a failed unit on a lower‑value F85/F86 example or for those with a limited budget. However, used M‑division V8s carry significant risk: you don't know the engine's service history, oil consumption patterns, valve stem seal condition, or whether the cooling system has been stressed. Only consider a used unit with full service history, an oil analysis report, and a compression test from a BMW M specialist. Expect to pay £4,500-£7,500 for a used S63B44T2.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most S63B44T2 replacements, a professionally reconditioned unit is the right call. A proper recon addresses the engine's known weak points: the cooling system (water pump, thermostat) is overhauled, the turbochargers are inspected and rebuilt if necessary, the valve stem seals are replaced, and all gaskets and seals are renewed. With a 12‑24 month warranty, this is the lowest‑risk option for a £7,500-£12,000+ investment.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for this engine only when the original block is in good condition and the vehicle has significant sentimental or collector value - e.g. a low‑mileage F85 X5 M or a well‑specified F86 X6 M. A performance‑oriented rebuild can include upgraded forged internals and larger turbos, but for most owners, a reconditioned exchange unit offers better value and less downtime. Expect £10,000-£16,000+ for a full rebuild.

items.answer: A reconditioned S63B44T2 costs £7,500-£12,000+ supply‑only, plus £1,050-£1,530 for fitting at a specialist M‑approved workshop. Used units start from £4,500, and full rebuilds range from £10,000-£16,000+. items.question: What are the common problems with the S63B44T2?
items.answer: The most frequently reported issues are oil leaks from valve cover gaskets (due to the hot‑vee design), cooling system stress, and valve stem seal wear causing oil consumption and blue smoke on startup. The T2 revision improved connecting rod lubrication and the oil pump intake for track use, but heat‑related issues remain the primary concern. Regular oil level checks between services are essential. Cooling system inspection should be part of every service on high‑mileage examples.

items.question: Which BMW models have the S63B44T2 engine?
items.answer: The S63B44T2 is fitted exclusively to the F85 X5 M (2015-2018) and F86 X6 M (2015-2019), producing 567-575 bhp. It is the second Technical Update of the S63 V8 and was the most powerful engine BMW had fitted to an all‑wheel‑drive vehicle at the time of its release. It replaced the S63B44T1 used in the F10 M5 and F12/F13 M6. It was superseded by the S63B44T3 in the F90 M5 and subsequent models.

Used units are cheaper but carry unknown history; full rebuilds are justified only for high‑value or heavily modified cars. Reconditioned from £7,500; used from £4,500; rebuilt from £10,000. items.question: How do I tell the S63B44T2 apart from other S63 variants?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on a metal plate on the driver's side of the cylinder block, and appears on the V5C and in the VIN (digits 4‑7). The S63B44T2 is the 2015‑2019 generation used in F85/F86 X5 M/X6 M; it differs from the S63B44T1 (F10 M5/F13 M6) by having revised connecting rods and a track‑optimised oil pump intake. The S63B44T3 (2018‑present) is the latest version with higher output. Do not confuse it with the standard N63B44 (non‑M) or the S63B44O0 (earliest generation). Fitting the wrong generation can cause ECU mismatches, engine mount issues, and cooling system incompatibilities.
bullets: Do not confuse it with the standard N63B44 (non‑M) or the S63B44O0 (earliest generation).

items.question: How reliable is the S63B44T2 compared to the N63?
items.answer: The S63B44T2 is significantly more robust than the standard N63, thanks to its forged internals, improved lubrication system, and track‑specific oil pump design. However, the hot‑vee architecture means heat‑related issues - particularly oil leaks and cooling system stress - are common across both engine families. The S63B44T2 addressed many of the early N63's bearing and timing chain concerns, but diligent maintenance remains essential. Regular servicing (every 8,000 miles or annually) is critical. If you track the car, consider upgraded cooling components and more frequent oil changes.
